species.name: Cape Honey Badger
species.description: Average-sized subspecies found across southern and southwestern Africa.

daily_routine.detail: Active at random times both day and night

species.preferred_biomes: Forests, grasslands, steppes, rocky hills and deserts (almost anywhere)

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Males are larger and weigh almost twice as much as females.

variations.age: Young animals are more playful and less aggressive.

behavior.detail: Non-migratory, lives in a smaller range

species.trivia: Honey badgers raid beehives for honey and larvae, shrugging off stings from aggressive bee swarms.

species.name: Common Hippopotamus
species.description: Wide-ranging subspecies, from northern Africa to Gambia and Ethiopia; its skull has a somewhat shorter preorbital region than other subspecies.

daily_routine.detail: Active at dusk, night and dawn

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Bulls have slightly bigger bodies and tusks, and much heavier jaws.
sex_differences.other: Apart from slight size differences, bulls and cows look alike.

behavior.detail: Non-migratory, focused on protecting its territory

species.trivia: Turtles and young crocodiles sometimes bask on top of hippos.

species.name: Cape Mountain Zebra
species.description: The smallest zebra subspecies, found in some mountainous regions of eastern and southern Africa.
species.preferred_biomes: Slopes and plateaus of mountainous areas

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Size differences are inconsistent; either sex can be larger.
sex_differences.other: Stallions have a more prominent dewlap (loose skin under the neck).

behavior.detail: Moves between higher and lower altitudes

species.trivia: Zebras see well both by day and at night.

species.name: Northwestern White-tailed Deer
species.description: The biggest and darkest White-tailed deer subspecies.
species.preferred_biomes: Forests, grasslands, swamps and arid areas with dense thickets

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Bucks are noticeably larger and about half again as heavy as does.
sex_differences.other: Bucks have antlers and are more often solitary.

variations.age: Younger deer can have spotted coats.
variations.coat_colors: Light reddish brown to dark grayish-brown, depending on season and environment

weaknesses: Vulnerable to callers and scents during the rut
recommended_equipment: Primos The Great Big Can Doe Bleat

behavior.detail: Does not stay in one territory

species.trivia: White-tailed deer swim well and use wide streams and lakes to escape predators.

aggression.source: Community notes (not yet checked in game)
aggression.wiki_check: Both wikis say only Southern lion, Common hippopotamus and Cape buffalo charge the player in 1.0, so this aggression note is likely wrong.

species.name: Rocky Mountain Mule Deer
species.description: The most widespread Mule deer subspecies, from the northern US Southwest up to northern Canada.
species.preferred_biomes: Forests, grasslands, arid areas and mountains (highly adaptable)

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Bucks are much larger than does.
sex_differences.other: Bucks grow antlers for competition and display.

variations.age: Older animals carry their heads low with hackles raised.

strengths: Agile, capable of quick, erratic and swift movements
recommended_equipment: Primos The Great Big Can Doe Bleat

behavior.detail: Moves between higher and lower altitudes

species.trivia: Mule deer can sense water about two feet below ground.

aggression.source: Community notes (not yet checked in game)
aggression.wiki_check: Both wikis say only Southern lion, Common hippopotamus and Cape buffalo charge the player in 1.0, so this aggression note is likely wrong.

species.name: Blesbok
species.description: A bontebok subspecies of South Africa, Namibia and Eswatini that sticks to open grasslands close to water.

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Males are larger and sturdier, with longer, thicker horns.

variations.coat_colors: Brown body with white facial blaze, belly and legs

weaknesses: Dependence on water sources and herd instincts make them predictable

behavior.detail: Does not stay in one territory

species.trivia: Heavy hunting once left only 17 wild bontebok.

species.name: Spotted Hyena
species.description: An African hyena with an unusually complex, female-led social hierarchy and fierce competition within the species.

daily_routine.detail: Active at dusk, night and dawn

species.preferred_biomes: Semi-deserts, savannas and mountain forests; avoids dense and coastal rainforests

sex_differences.other: Females are dominant and more aggressive.

behavior.detail: Non-migratory, focused on protecting its territory

species.trivia: Hyena fossils exist on four continents, but spotted hyenas have lived only in Africa for about the last 8,000 years.

species.name: Nile Crocodile
species.description: One of Africa's largest freshwater apex predators: very aggressive, agile and responsible for many human deaths each year.

daily_routine.detail: Active at dusk, night and dawn

species.preferred_biomes: Broad rivers, lakes and marshes next to open savanna, semi-desert and woodland

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Males are 20-33% larger and much heavier than females.
sex_differences.other: Apart from size, males and females look alike.

variations.coat_colors: Olive green to dark brown with darker bands on back and tail

weaknesses: Relatively low speed and agility on land

behavior.detail: Non-migratory, lives in a smaller range

species.trivia: Adult crocodiles help their young hatch out of their eggs.

species.name: Blue Wildebeest
species.description: The more common wildebeest subspecies, ranging north beyond South Africa; often interbreeds with the smaller Black wildebeest.
species.preferred_biomes: Savannas and open woodlands with fast-regrowing grass and moderate moisture

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Males are larger with thicker horns.
sex_differences.other: Otherwise the sexes differ only in size and coloring.

variations.age: Adults usually have darker coats with stronger stripes.
variations.coat_colors: Blue-gray or dark brown to black

behavior.detail: Moves between territories and defends each one

species.trivia: Some wildebeest have been seen chasing predators.

species.name: Rocky Mountain Elk
species.description: Found only in the Rocky Mountains and nearby mountain areas; chronic wasting disease is one of its biggest threats.
species.preferred_biomes: Open woodland at any elevation and swamps; avoids dense forest

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Bulls are larger and much heavier than cows.
sex_differences.other: Bulls have antlers and are more often solitary.

variations.coat_colors: Reddish-brown to dark brown or gray

weaknesses: Reliance on open areas for feeding

behavior.detail: Moves between higher and lower altitudes

species.trivia: In hot weather elk stay near water and wade or lie in it to cool off and avoid biting insects.

species.name: Northwestern Wolf
species.description: Western North American subspecies, considered the world's largest Gray wolf.

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Males have thicker necks, bigger foreheads and shoulders, and slightly longer legs.
sex_differences.other: Males tend to be more aggressive.

variations.age: Pack discipline gets better with age.
variations.coat_colors: White, gray, shades of brown, black

strengths: Difficult to isolate from strong packs
weaknesses: Likely to investigate baits and calls

behavior.detail: Covers wide ranges and defends its territory

species.trivia: Gray wolves feed pups by bringing swallowed food back up for them.

species.name: Wood Bison
species.description: The bigger American Bison subspecies, with a taller, squarer hump.
species.preferred_biomes: Grasslands at low and high elevations

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Bulls are 33-50% larger than cows, with bigger horns, blockier heads, thicker necks and larger humps.
sex_differences.other: Bull horns curve outward; cow horns curve inward.

variations.age: Adults develop a bigger hump and larger horns.
variations.coat_colors: Dark brown to black, lighter on the hindquarters

strengths: Massive size, with the ability to charge
weaknesses: Difficulty moving due to its size

behavior.detail: Migrates now and then over wide ranges

species.trivia: A bison's coat insulates so well that snow can sit on its back without melting.

aggression.charge_trigger: Approaching herd within 50m, wounding lead bull, or blocking movement
aggression.source: Community notes (not yet checked in game)

species.name: Rocky Mountain Pronghorn
species.description: Lives in the Rocky Mountain foothills, even though it generally dislikes rugged terrain.

sex_differences.size_and_weight: Males are slightly larger and heavier.
sex_differences.other: Females have small, sometimes barely visible horns; males have larger lyre-shaped horns, a black face mask and black neck patches.

variations.age: Adults are faster and have more stamina.

behavior.detail: Moves between territories and defends each one

species.trivia: Pronghorns can spot movement about 3 miles (4.8 km) away.

species.description: The second-largest moose subspecies, found in western Canada, the sub-Arctic and some northern US states.
species.preferred_biomes: Moist forests, in swamps or near lakes and ponds
species.trivia: Moose are usually slow and calm but can turn aggressive and fast when angered or startled.

harvest_ranking.explanation: Each species is scored on its own trophy type (antlers, horns, tusks, skull, weight or body length). A harvest report shows the measurements, each with points, adding up to a Total Trophy Score. It also gives a Hunt Rating (letter grade for shot quality, e.g. S++), a 1-5 star Trophy Rating, and a sell price based on dressed weight.

stewardship_levels.status_desc: Habitat neglected. Heavy inbreeding and poor genetics dominate the herds.
Genetic potential compromised. Aggressive culling of low-tier males required.
Baseline ecosystem health. Feeders and clean water will elevate the herd.
Strong genetics. 3-star and 4-star trophies appearing regularly.
Elite ecosystem. Habitat enhancements active; 5-star trophies spawn consistently.

interventions.culling_quota: Remove at least 2 mature males under 55% fitness per generation to lift regional average.
interventions.pollution_removal: Eliminating toxic runoffs (e.g., Lake Sasquatch) unlocks the genetic ceiling for all surrounding herds.
interventions.feeder_installation: Mineral feeders provide consistent nutrition, shielding young animals from genetic stalls during harsh weather.

fitness_advisor.label: Inferior Genetics
fitness_advisor.action: Cull. Remove to stop weak genetics passing to future generations.

fitness_advisor.label: Moderate Genetics
fitness_advisor.action: Average herd member. Let it reach adult; cull if male trophy potential stalls.

fitness_advisor.label: Superior Genetics
fitness_advisor.action: Do not harvest early. Let it reach the oldest mature age for 5-star potential.

sections.title: Match your shot to the animal
sections.body: Way of the Hunter 2 does not use the first game's 'ammo tier' numbers. Each animal has a class (1 = smallest, 9 = biggest) and a recommended bullet energy in joules (J) at the moment of impact. Pick a gun and ammo whose energy at your shooting distance falls inside that range. Too little energy gives a wounded animal and a long blood trail; far too much ruins the meat and lowers the harvest score. Shotguns list a distance range instead (buckshot / slug), and 'Inappropriate' means do not use it on that animal.
bullets: Check the energy number on the ammo in the weapon screen; it drops the farther away the animal is.
Aim for the heart/lungs; a clean hit gives a better harvest rating and more credits.
Class 8-9 (moose, bison, crocodile, hippo) need the heaviest rifles; the hippo, lion and Cape buffalo can charge you.

sections.title: Trophy stars (1 to 5)
sections.body: Trophy rating comes from fitness, age and trophy size together.
bullets: 1 star: young, weak or average; only shoot to cull the herd.
2-4 stars: growing or mid animals; protect the good genetics, cull the poor ones.
5 stars: the best trophies, usually the result of managing a herd over time (use the Watchlist to time it).

sections.title: Leveling, credits and skill points
bullets: Each level-up pays credits (800 at L14, 850 at L15, 950 at L17) and unlocks gear; the Wallet adds this for you.
A normal harvest gives about 70-100 XP; missions, NPC objectives and challenges give bigger one-time XP.

sections.title: Game time
bullets: 3 in-game days = 1 year for the animals; ages go up at midnight.
Put the in-game day and time into the Wallet so the Watchlist countdown stays right.
